title: fix(plugin-gantt): a silent re-read that overtakes a changed query takes over its report (objectui#10633)
body:
Fixes #10633

Clause-②: no

A silent re-read that overtakes a changed query still in flight now takes over that query's report. No prop, export or schema moves.

## What changed

`ObjectGantt`'s `reload()` lets only the newest run commit (`isCurrent()`), and the newest run's `silent` flag decided whether a failure reports. The data-invalidation bus, the toolbar refresh and the four write-readbacks all call `reload({ silent: true })`. Suppose one of them starts while a changed query (a sort, filter or search change: non-silent, in place) is in flight. It re-reads the changed query and makes the changed run stale, which discards the changed run's answer and its failure. When the silent run then failed, it only logged. The chart ended on the FIRST query's rows, with no error and no refreshing state. That breaks the objectui#7237 contract: a failed CHANGED query is reported, and the rows on screen answer the previous query.

Now a run owes a report when it is non-silent, or when it supersedes a run that still owes one (`reportOwedRef`, set when a run starts). The current run releases it when it settles, in the same `isCurrent()`-guarded `finally` that clears the loading flags. The `catch` now reports when the run owes a report, where before it reported when the run was non-silent. A standalone silent re-read (nothing pending) owes nothing and behaves as before: it logs a failure and keeps its rows.

Files:
- `packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.tsx`: `reload()` and its run bookkeeping only.
- `packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.silentOvertake-10633.test.tsx`: new, 9 cases.
- `.changeset/10633-gantt-silent-overtake.md`: `'@object-ui/plugin-gantt': patch`.

## Reproduction (the card's probe P1, re-run)

The probe used the real `ObjectGantt` and the real `notifyDataChanged`, in the root config's `dom` project. The sequence: first paint, then a sort change in flight, then an invalidation re-read that overtakes it. The two remaining settles were run in both orders: the stale changed query answers, and the re-read fails.

| Run | refreshing in flight | first-query rows | changed-query rows | error | refreshing at end |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base `f99f9cde7`, changed query answers, then the re-read fails | true | **true** | false | **false** | false |
| base, the re-read fails, then the changed query answers | true | **true** | false | **false** | false |
| head, both orders | true | false | false | **true** | false |
| base and head, a standalone silent re-read fails (control) | true | true | n/a | false | false |

The base rows match the card's reading exactly. The probe was a throwaway file and is not committed. The committed pins below carry the same sequences.

## Inherit or re-issue: inherit, and why

Both designs were measured against the 16 pins: this file's 9, plus the 7 of PR objectui#10630. Each alternative is a mutation of the committed head through `ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode. The anchor must hit, and the landing is proven by the anchor count and a blob change. The restore is proven by the blob equalling HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

| Design | Pins | Why |
|---|---|---|
| (a) inherit inside `reload()`: this PR | 16 passed | |
| (b1) the bus re-read re-issued at its call site as `{ inPlace: true }` while a report is owed | 1 failed: the toolbar refresh row | The toolbar refresh and the four write-readbacks call `reload({ silent: true })` themselves, so each would need the same re-issue. |
| (b2) re-issued inside `reload()` as a plain non-silent run | 2 failed: the chart is torn down (the `GanttView` instance reads `unmounted` in flight and `2` after) | `inPlace` defaults to `silent`, so a non-silent re-issue swaps in the loading placeholder after the first paint. objectui#7237 ruling A′ rules that out. |
| (b3) re-issued inside `reload()` as non-silent, with `inPlace` carried over | 16 passed | The same behaviour as (a), reached by rewriting `silent` and restructuring the signature. |

Chosen: **(a)**, the smallest change that holds every row: one ref and three lines in `reload()`. The obligation lives in the run sequence, which is where the supersession happens, so one site covers every silent caller. It does not touch the signature or the `inPlace` default.

## The refreshing state: a claim assumption that did not hold

The claim asked that the inheriting run "show the refreshing state", and that a standalone silent re-read have "no refreshing flash". On base, a silent run is always in place and sets `refreshing` when it starts. So the overtaking re-read already showed the refreshing state in flight (the probe's first column: true on base). A standalone silent re-read shows it too. This change leaves both as they are. The in-flight state is pinned: the chart stays mounted, no placeholder shows, and the refreshing state stays on after the stale changed query answers. The standalone control pins today's refreshing-while-in-flight, not the "no flash" that base does not have.

## Pins (`ObjectGantt.silentOvertake-10633.test.tsx`)

| Pin | base `f99f9cde7` | head | red under |
|---|---|---|---|
| the card's sequence: overtaken by an invalidation re-read that fails ⇒ reported (plus, in flight: the same chart, refreshing on) | RED | green | A0, b2 |
| the same, settled the other way round | RED | green | A0 |
| the overtaking re-read succeeds ⇒ the changed query's rows, no error, the same chart | green | green | b2 |
| the toolbar refresh overtakes the changed query and fails ⇒ reported | RED | green | A0, b1 |
| two re-reads in a row: the report passes down the chain | RED | green | A0, A3 |
| before the first paint: a re-read overtakes the initial load and fails ⇒ reported, not an empty chart | RED | green | A0 |
| control: a standalone silent re-read fails ⇒ quiet, the rows stay, the failure is logged | green | green | A1 |
| control: once the changed query has answered, a later re-read that fails stays quiet | green | green | A1 |
| control: a silent re-read overtakes another silent one and fails ⇒ quiet | green | green | A1, A2 |

On base, with `ObjectGantt.tsx` at `f99f9cde7` and the new pin file run against it: `Tests 5 failed | 4 passed (9)`.

## Ablations

Every leg ran on the committed source blob `79459f66bb80` and was restored to it, proven by blob and by an empty `git diff HEAD`.

- **A0**, the fix reverted (`reportsFailure = !silent`), on HEAD `8f20311d9`: `Tests 5 failed | 4 passed (9)`. The five overtaking rows go red and the four controls stay green.
- **A1**, the obligation never released (its `finally` line deleted): 4 failed. They are the three new controls, plus PR objectui#10630's "a SILENT reload that fails after an error leaves the error on screen".
- **A2**, inheriting from any pending run: 1 failed (the silent-over-silent control).
- **A3**, inheriting one level only: 1 failed (two re-reads in a row).

A1's first attempt was a no-op. Its replacement text sat inside the anchor, so the tool refused on its own disk check (replacement count 1 to 1) and no test ran. It was re-run in `--delete` mode, and the reading above is from that re-run.

A1 to A3 and b1 to b3 ran at `a918971fe`. `8f20311d9` adds only a type annotation to one predicate in the test file, and the source blob is the same at both.

## PR objectui#10630's pins

`ObjectGantt.errorClears-10578.test.tsx` passes 7 of 7 on head, and under every leg except A1 (above). Its "why the error is not cleared when a reload STARTS" case still holds: the overtaking re-read now reports its own failure there, and that case asserts "an error", not a text.

## Local verification (HEAD `8f20311d9`)

- Dependency closure built first: `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/plugin-gantt^...' --concurrency=2` gave `Tasks: 12 successful, 12 total`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-gantt/` from the repo root: `Test Files 79 passed (79)`, `Tests 604 passed (604)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-gantt type-check`: exit 0, with the script name echoed. The new test is in the `tsconfig.test.json` program (`--listFilesOnly`: 1 hit). The first run was red on TS7031, an implicit-any binding in the new test; `8f20311d9` repairs it.
- Gates, each exit 0:
  - `check:control-bytes`: OK.
  - `check:new-line-citations`: "VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)".
  - `check-changeset-presence`: "2 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)".
  - `changeset:check` (the fixed group and no-major), `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`.
  - `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:test-path-roots`.
- `check:changeset-claims` (report-only): two pending changesets name `ObjectGantt.tsx`. `6475-gantt-block-face-declared` is about `getGanttConfig`'s keys, and `6939-objectql-record-source-refinement` is about `getDataConfig`'s resolution order. I read both paragraphs. This diff touches neither function, so both still hold.
- ESLint: the per-package `eslint .` that `pnpm lint` runs through turbo, from `packages/plugin-gantt`, with `--format json`, over 2 files.
  - `ObjectGantt.tsx` has the same per-rule counts as the base blob, piped through `--stdin-filename` at the same path. All are warnings and neither side has an error; `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` is 1 on both sides.
  - The new test has 7 `no-explicit-any` warnings, the same stand-in shape as the sibling pin files.
  - `eslint.config.js` declares no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot change the verdict on any untouched file.
- Governed surface: `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` reports NOT GOVERNED for all 3 paths.

## Siblings with the same shape: none

Outside `ObjectGantt.tsx`, every non-comment `silent` hit in `packages/plugin-*/src` is prose. As a control, the same `git grep` returns 8 non-comment hits in `ObjectGantt.tsx`. No sibling view has a silent reload mode, which agrees with the card: `ObjectGrid` has none.

## Acceptance notes

- Unchanged: suppose the stale changed query answers with rows and then the overtaking re-read fails. Those rows answer the same current query, read before the write, but they are discarded under the existing sequencing and the error shows. Letting a stale run commit when its query equals the current one would take a query-key comparison. That is a third design, neither of the two the card named, and it is not done here.
